lede: A Chennai cargo airline that grew revenue twelvefold in four years flying leased Boeing 737 freighters to South-East Asia, the Maldives and the Gulf, with 40% EBITDA margins. The ambition is a nine-aircraft fleet including wide-body 777s, but aircraft have repeatedly arrived later than promised, and FY26 revenue fell well short of the targets management set.

short_version.text: FY26 revenue ₹583 Cr (+144%) and PAT ₹122 Cr (+230%) on just two aircraft, utilisation of 9-11 hours a day, yields above the IATA average, and Designated Indian Carrier status that cuts fuel cost 5-7%. Q1 FY27 revenue +49% with a 41% EBITDA margin; ~₹479 Cr raised since listing funds the fleet plan.

Targets of ₹1,000 Cr, then ₹700 Cr, for FY26 were missed; the fourth and fifth 737s promised 'before the next quarter' in June were still only 'planned' at the September AGM, and the 777s became a 'future strategy'. March-quarter profits were boosted by war charters, and the business has burnt cash over five years.
~30x trailing earnings and ~19x EV/EBITDA, about double the QIP price of ₹760 in May 2026. Blue Dart trades at 34x; there is no listed pure cargo airline in India.

blocks.text: AFCOM flies international air cargo from Chennai using leased Boeing 737-800 converted freighters (about 20-24 tonnes each), selling capacity by weight or as whole-aircraft charters through its general sales agent TTK Group to forwarders such as DHL, Kuehne+Nagel and DSV. Routes cover Singapore, Bangkok, Hanoi, the Maldives, Sri Lanka and, since FY26, Dubai.

items.text: High aircraft utilisation (up to 11.5 hours a day) and charters lift revenue per trip.
Fuel is passed through as a surcharge; leases and maintenance reserves are the main fixed costs.
Designated Indian Carrier status exempts ATF from Tamil Nadu VAT.
Listed on BSE SME in August 2024 (₹74 Cr IPO); revenue from ₹48 Cr (FY22) to ₹583 Cr (FY26).
Raised ~₹205 Cr in a preferential issue with warrants (Dec 2025) and ₹200 Cr in a QIP (May 2026).
Moved to Ind AS in FY26: aircraft leases now on balance sheet (₹338 Cr), so EBITDA is not comparable with earlier years.

blocks.text: India has no other listed freighter airline; Blue Dart runs its own freighters inside an express-logistics business, and IndiGo carries cargo in passenger bellies and a few freighters. Foreign carriers dominate India's international cargo.

items.text: Five 737s plus two 777s flying in FY28: revenue ~₹1,800 Cr at a 20% PAT margin (₹360 Cr), valued at 25x.

items.name: Base
items.text: Fleet grows a year late: ~₹1,100 Cr revenue in FY28 at 18% (₹198 Cr), valued at 22x.

items.name: Bear
items.text: Fleet stuck at three or four and yields fall: ~₹750 Cr at 14% (₹105 Cr), valued at 15x.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

AFCOM's unit economics are impressive and it has the capital for its fleet plan. The problem is delivery: aircraft timelines have slipped repeatedly and the stock has doubled since the May QIP. The outcome hinges almost entirely on when the fourth, fifth and wide-body aircraft actually fly.
